results.title: Together Link Review: Setup, Models, and Beta Limits
results.content:
1. Task quality: Compare the selected model with the model your agent currently uses on the same bug-fix and refactoring tasks.
2. Routing behavior: Check whether automatic selection is predictable enough for your workflow; pin a model when it is not.
3. Cost behavior: Use the session receipt and `togetherlink usage` output, then compare the result with your own token budget.
4. Failure handling: Test what happens when a Together model is unavailable, rate-limited, or returns an error.
5. Data controls: Confirm Together’s current retention and privacy terms for the code and prompts you plan to send.
6. Rollback: Keep the native agent path available and verify that your original credentials, extensions, MCP servers, and session history still behave as expected.

## Together Link FAQ [...] ### Does Together Link replace my existing configuration?

The official description says the normal configuration remains untouched. Desktop applications use reversible profiles, but you should still verify the rollback path on your own machine.

### Is Together Link ready for production?

It is a beta. Use a controlled pilot if you need to evaluate it, and keep the native agent path for critical work until repository-level tests show that routing quality, billing, and failure recovery are acceptable. [...] ## Together Link FAQ

### Is Together Link free?

The launcher is presented as free and open source, but model inference is billed through Together AI using your API key. Free installation does not mean free coding-agent usage.

### Does Together Link work on Windows?

The current beta documentation lists macOS and Linux. Windows support is not documented, so Windows users should not assume compatibility.

### Which coding agents does Together Link support?

The documented environments are Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi Code, Claude Desktop including Cowork, and ChatGPT Desktop.

### Can I choose one model instead of using Auto?

Yes. The release documentation shows a `--main` option for pinning a model, and supported agents may also expose their own model-selection command.
